before_taxonomy.classification_basis: City dispatchers produced requests to move vehicles obstructing emergency response. The first-responder hotline stalled those requests on prolonged holds while obstructions persisted. A 40-minute ambulance delay and repeat relocation requests establish a material failure to deliver the signal in time for its required response. The internal queue or staffing fault remains unknown. Separately, the approved pre-incident adverse-event response commitment was not met by the usable emergency-assistance function during those obstructions.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: The approved March 2025 passenger safety plan specifies available adverse-event assistance and prompt roadside dispatch when autonomous operation cannot continue. City records describe repeated emergency requests stalled on hotline holds while vehicle obstructions persisted. These episodes establish a material shortfall in the required usable assistance function, independently of the power outage itself. No numerical hotline guarantee or finding about every stopped vehicle is inferred.

evidence_search.notes: Current screen reads the repository-preserved source-attributed evidence and complete episode inventory. It does not claim fresh full-text access to every originating source. No canonical restamp or independent source verification is implied.

episode_inventory.purpose: Preserve a source-specific paraphrase that links the primary occurrence evidence to VIGIL's governance interpretation without treating taxonomy classification as source fact.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The March 2025 passenger safety plan sets out adverse-event support and roadside response; the Commission approved it effective May 19, before the December outage.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A pre-existing operational commitment supplies the standard against which the actual assistance function must be assessed. Publication and approval do not themselves establish performance.
clauses.adjudication_note: Antecedent obligation evidence, applied with the later emergency-response episodes.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The December 20 PG&E outage disabled traffic signals and disrupted the wider city.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Infrastructure failure is distinct from the autonomous fleet’s contribution.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo reports more than 7,000 dark-signal crossings and a simultaneous surge in discretionary confirmation requests.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Local conservative handling can create correlated shared-assistance demand.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The confirmation backlog delayed some vehicles and contributed to congestion.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Delayed assistance and congestion do not establish sole citywide causation or control non-activation.

clauses.source_paraphrase: At the substation response, firefighters diverted time to moving a Waymo that blocked arriving units.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Direct obstruction and responder diversion are separately evidenced effects.

clauses.source_paraphrase: An ambulance dispatched at 5:14 p.m. encountered a disabled Waymo. Staff requested relocation at 5:28 and an ETA at 5:55; arrival was delayed by 40 minutes.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: This timed emergency-service effect differs from citywide congestion and from the other fire responses.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The repeated assistance requests and reported forty-minute ambulance obstruction establish an ineffective recovery route for an emergency-dependent function. The approved pre-incident plan supplies the independent adverse-event response commitment.

clauses.source_paraphrase: A fire-response unit was blocked near Grant Avenue. Avoid-area messages were sent at 5:32 and 5:37 p.m.; a dispatcher seeking removal at 5:43 remained on hold at 5:53.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Produced protective requests require timely delivery to a capable response point.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: City dispatchers produced requests to move vehicles obstructing emergency response. The first-responder hotline stalled those requests on prolonged holds while obstructions persisted. A 40-minute ambulance delay and repeat relocation requests establish a material failure to deliver the signal in time for its required response. The internal queue or staffing fault remains unknown.

The dispatcher remained on hold while a fire-response unit was blocked; the required assistance function was not practically available in that episode. The approved pre-incident plan supplies the independent adverse-event response commitment.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Across overlapping emergency responses, dispatchers made 31 hotline calls totalling two hours and 36 minutes, mostly on hold. The Mayor contacted Waymo directly.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Aggregate calls contextualise the preceding responses; they are not 31 additional independently reconstructed obstructions.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The city reports prolonged holds on the designated response channel, with a separate mayoral escalation. Requests did not reliably reach timely disposition while the emergency obstructions required intervention.

The city reports prolonged hotline holds across emergency requests, corroborating material degradation of the assistance function, not merely an isolated bad message. The approved pre-incident plan supplies the independent adverse-event response commitment.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Seven reported immobilised Waymo obstructions affected Muni vehicles; one vehicle was delayed by 41 minutes.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Transit disruption is separate from fire, ambulance and hotline effects.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo paused service and directed vehicles to park and return to depots in waves. City reports continued after the reported 5:55 p.m. suspension.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Stopping new service and clearing existing obstructions are distinct protective effects.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The pause and retrieval were intended to reduce congestion and emergency obstruction. Later reports show remaining obstructions, but do not resolve the required clearance interval or each vehicle’s control and retrieval state. A bounded adequate-control outcome is therefore not established.

clauses.adjudication_note: The pause is established. Required clearing performance and the control state of each continuing obstruction remain unresolved.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On December 23, Waymo said outage-context updates were rolling out and that it would improve protocols, city coordination and responder training.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An announced rollout or plan is distinct from verified implementation and effectiveness.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The February city filing sought resilience planning, agency consultation, exercises and access to stoppage data; it cited 1,593 provider-reported stoppages among 829 vehicles.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Later review and aggregate disclosure are distinct from the December operational responses. The city’s estimates and requests are not regulatory findings.

notes: Retain existing current-edition findings. The pre-event plan and material response delays are the basis; no invented numerical universal SLA. Seven-thousand successful crossings do not erase specific obstructions, and the citywide blackout is not attributed solely to Waymo. Post-pause reports remain separate from announcement of future measures.

failure_recognition.condition: A material governance signal, decision, advisory, or escalation is produced.
failure_recognition.assessment: Dispatchers requested vehicle relocation and supplied avoid-area messages.

failure_recognition.condition: The signal must reach a capable decision, execution, or review point to have its required effect.
failure_recognition.assessment: The requests needed a capable Waymo response/relocation endpoint.

failure_recognition.condition: The signal terminates, stalls, or reaches only an incapable destination before that effect occurs.
failure_recognition.assessment: Long hotline holds stalled the requests while emergency obstructions persisted.

success_recognition.condition: A governance signal requires a response or disposition.
success_recognition.assessment: Emergency obstruction signals required timely response.

success_recognition.condition: Accountable ownership, a capable destination, status and escalation remain established until the required effect or authorised disposition occurs.
success_recognition.assessment: The prolonged holds did not maintain a capable timely disposition path.

success_recognition.condition: Delivery, ownership and response evidence traces the signal through to its bounded disposition.
success_recognition.assessment: Repeated calls and delayed ambulance/fire response contradict timely delivery for the bounded incidents.

exclusions.condition: The signal reaches a capable destination and is deliberately rejected through an authorised decision.
exclusions.assessment: The signals were not deliberately rejected through a justified decision.

exclusions.condition: No governance signal was produced because the control failed to activate.
The signal has operational effect but its delivery is not recorded for audit.
exclusions.assessment: Actual prolonged holds are documented, not only missing audit records.

failure_recognition.condition: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.
failure_recognition.assessment: The approved pre-event passenger safety plan established adverse-event support and roadside response for the service.

failure_recognition.condition: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
failure_recognition.assessment: The emergency assistance function degraded under the outage/confirmation backlog.

failure_recognition.condition: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
failure_recognition.assessment: The plan required usable support and a proportionate response to obstructing vehicles, including adverse events.

failure_recognition.condition: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.
failure_recognition.assessment: Repeated relocation requests and prolonged hotline waits failed to provide timely usable assistance during emergency obstruction.

failure_recognition.condition: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
failure_recognition.assessment: The ambulance/fire/Muni delays demonstrate impaired dependent emergency/transit functions.

success_recognition.condition: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
success_recognition.assessment: The approved response commitment was engaged by outage-related immobilisation.

success_recognition.condition: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
success_recognition.assessment: The observed assistance/backlog did not provide timely sufficient recovery for those obstructions.

success_recognition.condition: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
success_recognition.assessment: Later pause/retrieval and announced improvements do not establish the required usable support held at the time.

exclusions.condition: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
exclusions.assessment: The pre-event approved plan supplies an independent basis, beyond inconvenience or harm.

exclusions.condition: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
exclusions.assessment: The defect is service-function backlog/assistance, not one inaccurate output.

exclusions.condition: For failure-occurrence admission: a lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
exclusions.assessment: A valid outage pause does not justify the distinct unmet roadside-response commitment.

exclusions.condition: For failure-occurrence admission: a temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement, or an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
exclusions.assessment: The material emergency delays show the response did not meet the bounded obligation; no claim assumes all blackout effects were preventable.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
exclusions.assessment: The function itself was impaired, not only described inaccurately.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
exclusions.assessment: No identity/license verification dependency caused the problem.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
exclusions.assessment: No lost work-state mechanism alone explains it.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
exclusions.assessment: No access coercion or compelled concession is involved.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
exclusions.assessment: This is an operational emergency-support function, not solely an interaction-level vulnerability response.
